pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Headteacher - Bishopshalt School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
Welcome to Bishopshalt. It is with real pride that I am able to welcome you to our wonderful school, and do hope that you find all that you need within this website.
Bishopshalt is proud of its history, we retain its original mission and ensure that Bishopshalt is above all else a place for learning. We have the highest expectations of our students, and of ourselves as we believe that with high expectations students can achieve anything. All curriculum and leadership decisions are driven through our core values, focusing at all times at what is best for the students.
We believe that school is preparation for life, so on top of having the highest of expectations we also provide a wide curriculum that is designed to give students a breadth of educational experiences that enable them to excel in various fields and therefore open up future possibilities. This belief is lived and breathed through the Bishopshalt values.
We believe that relationships are also key to ensuring students reach their potential, and as staff it is our moral imperative to ensure that we act as role models and develop our relationships with the children in our care.
At Bishopshalt, we are driven by our core values. We believe wholeheartedly that with commitment and dedication all students that attend Bishopshalt will leave us at the end of Year 13 as well rounded citizens, able to compete on the world stage and have the brightest of Futures.
Mr L McGillicuddy
History
Bishopshalt opened in 1907 when Middlesex County Council established Uxbridge County School (our original name). The school now occupies the site and grounds of a former Victorian mansion and its name was taken from the house where, for 500 years, the Bishops of Worcester rested or halted in their own property while making frequent trips to and from London.
Bishopshalt's story is one of continuing growth and success; at first, as a grammar school and, since 1977 as a comprehensive school.
Much of the main part of the school building dates from the 1950's when the school grew to take four forms of entry each year. It has been a popular local secondary school and in the 1970's expansion to five forms of entry brought another building programme. Following the high demand for places, further growth took place in 1989 when the first six forms of entry arrived. An important ingredient in achieving growth and success is the quality of the teachers. Bishopshalt has always had a highly experienced, well qualified and very loyal staff. Since 1907 there have been just eight headteachers. Over the years many teachers have stayed to give the bulk of their professional service to the school.
Commitment and a willing involvement in the School extends to non-teaching staff and to parents. Parents play a major role as Governors of the School.

pageCache.pageTitle: School Values and Ethos - Bishopshalt School
pageCache.text:
School Values and Ethos
Love Learning - To develop in students a love for learning. Bishopshalt students will thirst for knowledge due to the intrinsic joy that it brings.
Show Kindness - To develop and instill in our students the virtue of kindness. Our students do things for others for no personal gain.
Build Character - To develop in students the determination and dedication to succeed. Bishopshalt students are able to overcome any challenge that may come their way. Our students are focused, resilient and readily overcome adversity.
Chase Brilliance - To develop students who do not settle for 'it's good enough'. Bishopshalt students always aim to improve their work and aim for perfection due to their belief that they are entitled to be brilliant.
Bright Futures - To ensure that, for whatever field they choose to enter, Bishopshalt students succeed. Bishopshalt students will be the very best versions of themselves and compete on the world stage.

pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher's Information for Parents - Latest News - Bishopshalt School
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Information for Parents
Please note all communications below are sent via email.
Dear Parents and Carers,
End of Term Communication and Reminders for September 2026
As we reach the end of the academic year, I would like to take this opportunity to thank you all sincerely for your support of the school over the past year. The partnership between home and school is central to everything we achieve, and the cooperation, encouragement and goodwill shown by our parents and carers has made a real difference to our students and to the school community as a whole.
This academic year has been exceptional, not only in terms of our Ofsted outcomes but also in the commitment to learning and our core values that have been demonstrated by our students and staff alike throughout the year.
I have ended the academic year meeting with Y10 students and their parents over the last two days, which I have found immensely enjoyable. Regardless of the circumstances for these meetings, throughout it has been apparent that the students want to achieve the brightest of futures and with the support of the parents and the school we aspire for them to achieve this.
We are hopeful that our Year 11 and 13 cohort results in August will enable them to go on to the futures that they deserve.
Staffing Announcement:
I am delighted to announce that Mrs Denial has been appointed Deputy Headteacher – Quality of Education. Mrs Denial will take up this role from September and will lead on the continued development of teaching, learning and the curriculum across the school. I know you will join me in congratulating her on this appointment.
As you will be aware from our previous communications, over the summer holidays our Year 10, and 12, students should be completing a minimum of 2 hours or revision a day over the holidays. The transition into your final year of study for GCSE and A level is vital to the individual students final success. We recognise the importance of resting and relaxation and this should be balanced with continuing to study during the holiday period.
Start of the New Academic Year:
The new academic year begins with:
Reminders for the New Term:
Please take careful note of the following reminders ahead of September:
We would like to invite you to attend these important meetings which will take place in school on the following dates:
Year 7 Thursday 3rd September - 1:45pm
Year 8/9 Thursday 10th September - 4:45 to 5:30pm
Year 10/11 Thursday 10th September - 6:00 to 6:45pm
Year 12 Thursday 8th October - 5:15 to 6:00pm
I would like to take this opportunity to reiterate the importance of excellent attendance. There is a clear and well-evidenced link between attendance and achievement, and every school day matters. We ask that all parents and carers continue to work cooperatively with the school to ensure that students attend every day, arrive on time, and are ready to learn. Where difficulties arise, please contact us at the earliest opportunity so that we can work together to support your child.
We remind all parents that holiday during term time will not be authorised. Where students are absent for unagreed periods, they will be required to catch up on all work that is missed during the absence. On their return to school they will attend after school sessions until 5:30pm each evening until the work that has been missed is completed and signed off by their teachers.
It remains only for me to wish all of our families a restful and enjoyable summer break.
We look forward to welcoming our new Y7 and 12 cohorts on Thursday 3rd and all of our students back to school on Friday 4th September 2026.
_____________________________________________________________________________
Dear Parents and Carers,
As we move towards the final half term of the academic year, I would like to thank you for your continued support and partnership with the school community.
We are incredibly proud to share the exceptional outcome of our recent Ofsted inspection. The school received seven “Exceptional” judgements, and we are in receipt of the first published report in England to achieve this under the new framework. This achievement reflects the hard work, dedication and commitment of our students, staff, governors and families, and we are delighted that the exceptional quality of education and care provided at the school has been recognised nationally. I could not have been more proud of our community demonstrating the core values which are central to all that we do.
Our Year 11 and Year 13 students are now fully underway with their GCSE and A Level examinations. We wish them every success during this important period and thank parents and carers for the support you continue to provide at home, which is particularly important from this point forward as students can now only attend for exams if they wish to do so. We have study facilities available for them in school and details have been shared with regard to this. Please refer to the Exams Timetable which can be found on the school website.
For the remaining cohort, the summer assessments for students in Years 7, 8, 9, 10 and 12 will begin on Monday 22 June through to Friday 3rd July. These assessments are an important opportunity for students to demonstrate their progress and help inform future learning. The timetables have been emailed to all parents and can also be found on the school website.
Attendance at school every day remains vitally important. Excellent attendance has a direct impact on students’ academic achievement, wellbeing and future outcomes. Conversely, non-attendance can have a significant detrimental effect on students’ progress and final results. We ask for your continued support in ensuring students attend school every day and arrive punctually.
This is important for all students across the school, not just Y10 and 12 who are midway through their respective GCSE/A Level courses, but also Y9 who are about to commence their GCSEs and Y7/8 who continue to build the vital learning to support their futures. If a student is absent from school for an extended period of time, we remind you that they are required to attend the catchup sessions which run Monday to Thursday 3:30 to 5:30pm, until all of the work that they have missed is completed and signed off by their teachers. We aim to ensure that students do not get left behind with their education and we will support them as they progress towards the brightest of futures.
The final Chase Brilliance term ahead is another busy and exciting one, with many opportunities for students to enrich their educational experience. Key dates include:
Please also take time to read this term’s edition of The Mitre Newsletter, which highlights the many fantastic events, achievements and activities that our students have participated in throughout the Spring Term.
We hope that we will see some warmer weather next term and would like to remind parents and carers of our expectations regarding school uniforms, in particular, girls’ skirts.
Skirts must be of an appropriate length and sit just above the knee and should not be of the fashion style lycra variety. Trousers should be school trousers or appropriate school-style trousers only. Items such as flares, palazzo pants, lycra bootleg leggings and skinny jeans are not permitted. Students not wearing the correct uniform will receive sanctions in line with the school behaviour policy.
From the next half term, students will also be permitted to wear school uniform shorts to school if they wish to do so. The shorts must be black, no cargo pockets, no branding, and specific to school wear. Sports, tie waist, fashion or any other variety of shorts will not be permitted:
Suggested Stockists:
Please note the shorts are unbranded and can be purchased from any store, as long as they are the appropriate style.
Both males and females may wear school shorts, with black or grey socks and their normal school shoes. Shorts must be worn with the normal shirt/tie or blouse and blazer. This summer uniform may be worn through to the October half term.
In a move towards sustainability, we encourage students to bring a reusable water bottle to school each day. This can be refilled from the school water fountains. We also advise students to apply sunscreen on warm and sunny days.
At the end of this term, we will say farewell to Ms Hubbard, Deputy Headteacher, who has been appointed as the new Headteacher of Chancellors School. We thank Ms Hubbard for her outstanding contribution to our school community and wish her every success in her new role.
We wish Eid Mubarak to the families celebrating Eid Al-Adha over the half term.
Finally, please be reminded that we return on Monday 1st June and the term will end on Friday 17th July, Progress Review Day, which students do not attend.
Thank you once again for your continued support. We look forward to a successful and productive final half term.
_____________________________________________________________________________
Dear Parents and Carers,
As we come to the end of this term, I would like to take a moment to thank you for your continued support and cooperation. It has truly been a fantastic term, filled with wonderful events and a great deal of effort and enthusiasm from our students. We are incredibly proud of all they have achieved.
During this term, we also welcomed Ofsted to the school. Unfortunately, we do not yet have the final report, but as soon as it is received, we will ensure it is shared promptly with parents and students. We do however have the first edition of The Mitre Newsletter.
Upon our return, Year 11 and Year 13 students will be commencing their Public Examinations. This is an important and focused time for them, and we ask for your support in reinforcing with all of our pupils the importance of respecting the rules and expectations of students who are not sitting exams around locations such as the main hall. Creating a calm and respectful environment is essential to help all students perform at their best.
For our Year 11 and Year 13 students, the upcoming break is a crucial period for study. It is vital that they use this time effectively by revising thoroughly, learning their notes, and completing as many past papers as possible. We strongly encourage students to maintain routines similar to the school day while at home, as this will help maximise the impact of their revision and preparation.
We would also like to remind all students and families of the importance of maintaining high standards of uniform. From the start of the summer term, heavy jackets/coats are no longer required, and at all times, both in school and on the journey to and from school, uniform should be of the highest standards. Students should bring in water bottles and ensure in the very hot days that they apply sun screen.
Over the next term there are many wonderful events to look forward to including Culture Day, Work Experience for Year 10 and 12, Chase Brilliance day and the various other end of Year celebrations. But above all, when we return we always focus on the core purpose of Bishopshalt, is that it is above all a place for learning.
I remind all parents that mobile phones should never be seen or heard whilst students are in school. They should be switched off as they arrive to the school site and not turned back on until they leave. At home, parents and carers should be tracking and monitoring what your children are accessing and doing online.
In line with our Behaviour for Learning Policy, Bishopshalt will not tolerate poor behaviour online. We are preparing children for life, and we will not allow students to be mean or unkind either in school or online. Beyond that safety is always our primary concern; it is important that you, as parents and carers, know who your children are communicating with when they are using their technology. Where there are instances of bullying and harassment, and these are reported to and investigated by the school, we will continue to keep phones for extended periods if students do not use them appropriately.
From the start of the new term, Year 8, like the years above them, will now have higher expectations of them in lessons and will only have Warning 1 before Oncall. This will ensure that lessons remain disruption free and students are always able to focus on their learning.
Year 9 Options will be finalised ahead of the Summer Holidays. As with each year we do have to ensure courses are viable and staffing is appropriate to ensure students succeed.
Thank you once again for your ongoing support. We hope you and your families have a restful and enjoyable break. We wish our Christian families a very happy Easter, and to all families, a restful and rewarding time.
We look forward to welcoming students back to school on Tuesday 21st April 2026.

Your encouragement and engagement with the school community are greatly appreciated by staff and students alike. We look forward to sharing the outcome of the inspection with you in the near future. Curriculum Subjects & Assessment
At Bishopshalt Sixth Form, our curriculum is broad, rigorous and inspiring. We believe in giving every student the knowledge, skills and confidence to excel at the highest level. At Bishopshalt, A Levels are the foundation - opportunity, ambition, and excellence make the difference.
Discover the full range of exciting Sixth Form courses at Bishopshalt School by exploring our latest Prospectus below. Inside, you'll find detailed descriptions of our challenging curriculum, plus, get all the essential information on entry requirements for each subject—your pathway to a Bright Future starts here! [Latest Sixth Form Prospectus]
A Levels at the Core
Our main academic programme is built around a wide range of A Level courses across Mathematics, Sciences, Humanities, Arts, Languages and Social Sciences. This breadth allows students to design a programme that reflects their passions, supports their future ambitions and provides the depth of study required by top universities and employers.
AS Subjects for Breadth
Alongside A Levels, students can also opt for a range of AS subjects. These include the Extended Project Qualification (EPQ), French, Spanish, and Classics. This flexibility gives students the opportunity to broaden their studies, showcase intellectual curiosity and strengthen their university or apprenticeship applications.
Expertise and Excellence
Our teachers are subject specialists who bring passion and expertise into every lesson. With small classes, expert guidance and a culture of high expectations, students achieve mastery of their chosen subjects while developing critical thinking, creativity and independence.
Beyond the Classroom
An inspiring curriculum is not confined to timetabled lessons. Scholars and students alike extend their knowledge through academic societies, MOOCs, Future Fridays, enrichment activities and national competitions, ensuring that every learner is challenged, inspired and prepared for life beyond Bishopshalt.
Assessment and Examination Information
For all information on Sixth Form examinations, please click here.
For internal assessments information and timetables, please click here.
Subject Specifications for Revision
To help with your revision, you can find links to exam specification for all of our subjects in the document below:
A-Level-Subject-Exam-Specifications-1.pdf
National Competitions and Academic Challenge
As part of the Sixth Form curriculum at Bishopshalt, students are expected to engage in national academic and enrichment competitions aligned with the subject areas in which they thrive. These competitions form an important element of our commitment to stretch, scholarship, and super-curricular excellence, supporting both university applications and intellectual development beyond specifications.
Sixth Form Participation (Years 12 and 13)
Students in Years 12 and 13 are actively encouraged—and in many cases expected—to enter national competitions and Olympiads within their strongest disciplines. These competitions develop advanced problem-solving, subject mastery, academic resilience, and independent thinking, all of which are essential for competitive university pathways.
Examples of Sixth Form competitions include:
Participation is supported through subject extension groups, staff mentoring, competition preparation sessions, and, where appropriate, alumni guidance.

Leadership and Mentoring of Lower School Competitions
In addition to their own competitive participation, Sixth Form students play a key leadership role in supporting and mentoring younger pupils entering national competitions. This forms part of their leadership development and contribution to the wider school community.
Sixth Form students help to coach, mentor, and lead preparation sessions for lower school competitions such as:
V&A Innovate National Schools Challenge
Through this mentoring, Sixth Form students consolidate their own subject knowledge while developing leadership, communication, and coaching skills, supporting younger students to access high-level academic opportunities early in their school journey.

A Culture of Challenge and Aspiration
This structured approach ensures that academic competition is embedded within the Sixth Form curriculum, not as an add-on but as a core expectation. Students are challenged to aim high in their chosen disciplines, while also giving back through leadership and mentoring.
By the time students leave Bishopshalt, they do so with a strong record of national competition participation, leadership experience, and academic distinction, strengthening applications to highly selective universities and future pathways.

pageCache.pageTitle: Success for Bishophalt's Teenage Entrepreneurs - Latest News - Bishopshalt School
pageCache.text:
Success for Bishophalt's Teenage Entrepreneurs
Last week, our students were in the Houses of Parliament to impress celebrities and minsters judging the Young Enterprise's company's programme.
The company's programme sees secondary school students come up with an idea, create a product and run a real student business. Bishopshalt was part of a group of 20 students from 3 London schools who showed off their ideas to celebrities, ministers and judges including BBC The Apprentice UK star Tim Campbell, award-winning broadcaster and journalist Steph McGovern and Minister for Small Business and Economic Transformation Blair McDougall MP. The event was also featured in The Times on Friday 6 February (you can read the article below)
Bishopshalt entered two teams in to the competition. Alaesa Luxuries, which makes jewellery and accessories from bismuth crystals and GoFigr, a business making marine-themed desk pets and fidget toys from sustainable biodegradable plastic. We are delighted and very proud to announce that one of our teams, GoFigr, were the winners.
The winning team successfully manufactured 73 toys, selling 70 of them at Portobello market and at school with a total profit of £350. Gurkaram RS took on the role of chief executive for GoFigr, pitching the idea to the judges without a hint of nervousness and even making Tim Campbell, the first winner of The Apprentice, laugh. Gurkaram said that, following the win, the company is hoping to expand its product range. “Young Enterprise really utilises skills that you already have,” he said. “It gives you certain new skills, but it refines the old ones."
Congratulations to both our teams on their success and thanks to Mr Ahmed for his hard work with this initiative.

pageCache.pageTitle: Young Entrepreneurs visit 10 Downing Street - Latest News - Bishopshalt School
pageCache.text:
Young Entrepreneurs visit 10 Downing Street
Students from Bishopshalt School taking part in the Young Enterprise Company Programme enjoyed a memorable visit to 10 Downing Street after winning the organisation’s Pitch to Parliament competition earlier this year.
The group of 16- and 17-year-old students were invited to meet Varun Chandra, chief business adviser to the Prime Minister Keir Starmer after a visit was arranged by Blair McDougall, Minister for Small Business at the Department for Business and Trade, and his team.
During the visit, the students were given a tour of 10 Downing Street by staff, with the opportunity to see several historic rooms including the Cabinet Room, Winston Churchill’s reading chair, Margaret Thatcher’s “White Room”, and the dining room where Boris Johnson held his COVID-19 press briefings.
The highlight of the day was an hour-long discussion with Varun, himself a former Young Enterprise participant. He answered a wide range of thoughtful questions from the students, covering topics such as leadership, career inspiration, and the potential impact of artificial intelligence on the future economy.
The visit offered students a rare opportunity to engage directly with a senior government adviser and gain insight into how government and business can work together to support entrepreneurship.
Young Enterprise said the experience demonstrated the growing recognition of youth entrepreneurship and the important role young people will play in shaping the UK’s future economy.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bishopshalt School Achieves National Recognition for Outstanding Performance - Latest News - Bishopshalt School
pageCache.text:
Bishopshalt School Achieves National Recognition for Outstanding Performance
Bishopshalt School is proud to announce that it has been recognised by SSAT (The Schools, Students and Teachers Network) in this year’s Educational Outcomes Awards. This national award places the school among the highest-performing secondary schools in the country, based on the latest performance data.
Bishopshalt School was recognised for being in the top 10% of non-selective schools nationally for student attainment in the 2025 end of KS4 exams.
The awards are based on analysis from SSAT’s Educational Outcomes Database, which combines data from DfE and Ofsted to compare performance across all state-funded schools in the country. Receiving a SSAT Educational Outcomes Award is a significant achievement and reflects the dedication, expertise and commitment of the entire school community.
Sue Williamson, Chief Executive of SSAT, commented: “Congratulations to Bishopshalt School on winning an SSAT Educational Outcomes Award. This success is down to the superb learning and teaching, outstanding support and inspirational leadership of staff. You have made a huge difference to the lives of the young people in your school. Thank you.”
SSAT is a membership organisation, bringing together schools and academies from across the UK and globally committed to achieving deep social justice. SSAT offers insight and understanding into school practice and educational policy and research. Their professional development and school improvement programmes help leaders and teachers to further outcomes for all young people and develop leadership at all levels across the system.

pageCache.pageTitle: KS3 Bright Sustainable Futures Curriculum - Bishopshalt School
pageCache.text:
KS3 Bright Sustainable Futures Curriculum
Our Bright Sustainable Futures curriculum ensures students engage in the real world and one of the ‘biggest questions’ for their generation, by looking at sustainability across their curriculum. Through this curriculum, students will also work to develop their careers awareness and learn that sustainability is threaded through a vast array of career opportunities.
Students explore key concepts and skills across Geography, Science, Design Technology and RS, in terms of ways of seeing. These are the core subjects which link across this curriculum, but other subjects are also threaded through. The topics across these subjects are all explored through the lens of sustainability. In Year 7, students explore the biodiversity of our urban environment and they will design products which aim to improve this biodiversity, for example. All their learning is deepened through our Drop Down Days and field trips for each year group. Due to the success of this curriculum, Year 7 now have a discrete Bright Sustainable Futures and Bishopshalt Experience lesson once a week, where they have opportunities to deepen their knowledge and learn beyond the classroom.
We want our students to have fluid knowledge and to understand the interdependence of our subjects, while also ensuring they gain the cultural literacy they need to excel and have power and influence; or in other words, to have ‘Bright Futures’. Our Bright Sustainable Futures curriculum is an education beyond examination.

pageCache.text:
Announcements
Sept 2027 Entry - Sixth Form Open Evening
Bishopshalt School Sixth Form Open Evening for 2027 entry will be taking place on Thursday 15th October 2026 at 5.45pm for a 6pm start.
Bookings are not required for the Open Evening, however, there will be no parking available on site, therefore alternative means of transport should be considered. All students attending the Open Evening must be accompanied by a parent/carer.
Please keep checking the website for further details nearer the time and for notification of any changes. These will be the only dates that we offer and unfortunately, we cannot accommodate any ad hoc visits.
All students attending this event must be accompanied by a parent/carer
The 2027 Prospectus will be available here from 16th October and applications will also open on this day. Full details of the courses available and the prospectus, when available, can be found on the Sixth Form section of the website.

Careers
At Bishopshalt we believe that Careers education makes a major contribution in supporting pupils to reach their potential.
The school's Career Plan for 2026-27 can be found here. This is designed in line with the Gatsby Benchmarks and the CDI Career Development Framework, underpinned by progressive learning outcomes. Click here for overview
Our Careers Education, Information, Advice & Guidance Policy can be found here
The school measures and assesses the impact of the careers programme on pupils through the Future Skills Questionnaires and regular feedback from Student Voice.
There are two qualified Careers Advisers in school who pupils can meet with for advice and guidance about career pathways. All students will have a careers meeting in both KS4 and KS5. Appointments take place throughout the academic year and pupils can also request a meeting by emailing careers@bishopshalt.school
Pupils and their families can access further careers support from the National Careers Service and Prospects.
Skills England can also be used to explore entry pathways for a range of careers.
The Careers Lead is Mrs Magee, she can be contacted via email at careers@bishopshalt.school
Provider Access
Bishopshalt complies with Provider Access Legislation. This is facilitated through whole cohort assemblies, KS4 and KS5 Open Evenings, The Futures Friday Programme, Careers Day and the KS5 Apprenticeship Programme.
Parental Engagement
The school recognises that parental involvement in career planning and decision-making is important for young people and their families so a list of useful links and resources can be found on the right-hand menu.
Employer Engagement
Bishopshalt School is keen to engage with employers and alumni to enhance our pupils' knowledge and understanding of careers and the world of work. The Futures Friday Programme welcomes external speakers weekly to share their career journeys and insights. If you are willing to work with us please get in touch using the contact details above or click here to let us know your availability.
Our annual whole school careers day is taking place on Wednesday 27th January 2027. If you'd like to get involved please reach out.
Teacher Engagement
Teaching staff play an important role in developing student knowledge and awareness of careers through the Bishopshalt Experience.
